subtopics.title: The CPJ — Job, Documents and Columns

questions.question: The Cash Payments Journal records:
options: All payments made from the business bank account, in date order, for one month
All receipts and payments together
Only payments to suppliers of stock
The owner's personal spending

questions.question: The name column of the CPJ carries:
options: A description of the goods bought
The payee — the person or business the money went to
The bookkeeper's initials
The ledger folio number

questions.question: Under the perpetual inventory system, stock bought for resale is entered in:
options: A Purchases column, as in older textbooks
The Sundry accounts column, named 'Purchases'
The Trading Stock column — the asset loads directly at cost
The Wages column

subtopics.title: The Standard Payments — and the Drawings Trap

questions.question: Stock is bought from Coastal Wholesalers for R9 500 by EFT. The columns struck are:
options: Bank R9 500 and Sundries R9 500, detail Purchases
Bank R9 500 and Trading Stock R9 500
Trading Stock R9 500 only
Bank R9 500 and Wages R9 500

questions.question: New display shelving of R5 500 is bought for use over several years. It is classified as:
options: An expense, because money left the bank
Drawings, because the owner chose it
Trading stock, because it stands in the shop
An asset — entered in Sundries with the detail Equipment

questions.question: The owner transfers R2 500 to herself for personal use. The correct treatment is:
options: Sundries R2 500, detail Drawings — a reduction of owner's equity, never an expense
Wages R2 500, because the owner works in the store
Sundries R2 500, detail Rent expense
No entry, because it is personal money

questions.question: The test that sorts every payment into asset, expense or drawings is:
options: How large the amount is
Whether it was paid by EFT or cash
Did the business receive value, and how long does that value last?
Whether the payee is a regular supplier

subtopics.title: Totals, the Cross-Cast, and What Posts Where

questions.question: Trading Stock totalled R9 500, Wages R3 600 and Sundries R12 200. The cross-cast requires the Bank column total to be:
At month end the Bank column total of the CPJ is posted as:
options: A debit to Bank, because money is an asset
A credit to Bank — payments reduce the asset
A debit to Capital
A credit to Trading Stock

questions.question: Which internal control belongs to the payments system?
options: The person who approves a payment also captures it, to save time
EFT references may be reused within a month
Bank reconciliation is only needed at year end
Payments are made only against approved documents, with numbered sequential references

subtopics.title: The Petty Cash Journal and the Imprest System

questions.question: Under the imprest system with a R600 float, at any moment the tin must satisfy:
options: Cash in the tin plus vouchers equals exactly R600
Cash in the tin equals R600
Vouchers alone equal R600
Cash minus vouchers equals R600

questions.question: Month-end vouchers total R420: stamps R75, taxi R90, tea and coffee R140, cleaning R115. The restoration payment is:
options: R600, to refill the tin completely
R180, the cash still in the tin
R420 — the restoration always equals the voucher total
Whatever amount the petty cashier requests

questions.question: A tin holds R180 cash and R390 in vouchers against a R600 float. This shows:
options: The tin balances perfectly
R30 is missing — cash plus vouchers falls short of the imprest amount
The float must be increased
R30 too much was spent on stamps

questions.question: In the money-out diary, the first thing recorded about a payment is:
options: WHO was paid — payments are chased payee first
The profit made on the day
The colour of the receipt
The month-end total

questions.question: Stock and wages earn their own lanes in the diary because:
options: They are the largest amounts
The bank requires it
They are the constant, repeating payments of the business
They are the only payments with documents

questions.question: The money-out handshake says that:
options: The lanes plus the named visitors must add up to the Bank column total
The Bank column must equal last month's total
Wages must never exceed stock purchases
Every payment needs two signatures

questions.question: The R2 500 Lindi transferred to herself is drawings, not an expense, because:
options: It was paid late in the month
The store received nothing for it — the owner drew on her own stake
It was smaller than the rent
She paid it by EFT instead of cash

questions.question: If drawings hide inside the expenses, the year-end result is that:
options: Profit is overstated
The bank balance is wrong
The store's profit looks lower than it truly performed
The trial balance will not balance

questions.question: The shelving is also not a 'cost of the month' because:
options: It is a possession the store keeps and uses for years — an asset
It was bought on the 21st
The supplier delivered it for free
It appears in the Wages column

subtopics.title: The Tin That Always Tells the Truth

questions.question: Anyone taking money from the tin must leave behind:
options: An IOU note with their name
Nothing, if the amount is under R50
The exact change
A signed voucher stating what it was for and how much

questions.question: An afternoon count shows R260 cash and R310 in slips against a R600 float. The tin is telling you:
options: R30 is missing — and it is discovered today, not at year end
Everything balances
R30 too much cash is in the tin
The float should be raised to R630

questions.question: The month-end refill amount is set by:
options: Rounding the spending up to the nearest hundred
The voucher total — R420 refills exactly what the slips explain
The petty cashier's estimate
A fixed R600 payment every month
